title: HC Mike LaFleur Postgame Press Conference | Week 1 vs. Los Angeles Chargers
headline: Brissett's quick-release efficiency and passing targets (McBride, Harrison Jr., Bourne) drove the Week 1 win, but LaFleur flagged red-zone struggles and a running back returning from a long layoff.
summary: LaFleur called the Week 1 win over the Chargers a reward for a long camp and said the team needs to reset quickly for a strong next opponent. He credited the defense for its energy, conditioning, and resilience, especially in the second half, and praised its turnovers and pressure on the quarterback. On offense, he said Jacoby Brissett got the ball out quickly against pressure, and the receivers and tight end executed well in their transitions. He took personal blame for the scheme on a short-yardage keep and a red-zone call that led to an opponent blitz, and he said the red-zone failures left a lot of points on the field. He said the running backs started grinding out yards in the fourth quarter, and that a back who had not practiced in three or four weeks showed explosiveness on his first touchdown and should keep getting more conditioned. LaFleur also said the team had three pre-snap penalties on offense that need to be cleaned up, and he said the offense needs to get in and out of the huddle faster. He did not discuss betting odds and said the team would focus on process rather than results.

On the offense, he praised Jacoby Brissett's accuracy, his feet, and his quarterback sneaks, and said he had a few footwork and timing items to clean up with him. LaFleur said Jeremiyah Love's workload was mostly game-flow driven, with no formal pitch count, though the team was monitoring snaps after weeks away from practice, and he called the amount fair. He framed Tyler Allgeier and Love as different skill sets and said two-back looks could recur in future weeks. He said the red zone struggles (two of five) started with a play-call and protection issue he owns, and that Marvin Harrison Jr.'s target share was more about how the game unfolded than a plan. He said the team will reset and turn to Seattle, which is coming to Arizona for a home game.

Johnson credited the offensive line and receivers for a running game that gained nearly 300 yards, with Swift and Kyle Monangai both running hard, including a 60-yard run by Monangai. On the passing side, he discussed Caleb Williams' improved checkdown decisions and scrambling, and said Williams' two rushing touchdowns came from decisive reads. title: Todd Monken Press Conference : September 14th, 2026
headline: Monken confirmed Deshaun Watson as the starter for next week at Tampa Bay after reviewing the film, while calling the Week 2 offensive performance below standard. Dylan Sampson's injury is still being evaluated, with updates expected Wednesday.
summary: Monken called the film disappointing, saying the team's effort and physicality were fine but operational execution, communication, and complementary football were not, especially in the 18 to 20 minutes after a strong start. He said the offense couldn't get first downs or get off the field, and that the team needs to shrink its calls, get plays off faster, and manage the clock. He confirmed that Deshaun Watson will remain the starter, citing good practice reps and flashes on film while acknowledging that the operational issues fall on the coaching staff, the players, and Watson. On the run game, he said the team never got enough plays to build rhythm, with several three-and-outs and turnovers early. He praised the two rookie offensive linemen, saying Austin Barber will start and Spencer Fano will keep developing. On defense, he said tackling in the open field was fine and that he anticipates no personnel changes in the secondary. He said the injury evaluation of Dylan Sampson is ongoing, with more information coming Wednesday. He also addressed Denzel Boston's limited involvement, saying it wasn't by design and that penalties and missed looks reduced his targets. Finally, he responded to questions about Baker Mayfield and Mike Tomlin's comments, saying the team needs to own the loss and play better rather than accept the 'Browns being Browns' narrative.

title: Brian Schottenheimer: “Our Standards and Expectations Are High” | Press Conference
headline: Hooker (fracture, surgery Friday) and Overshown (hamstring strain, 1-2 weeks) are both expected to miss time, so Barham, James, and Barron pick up the linebacker snaps, while Downs stays near the line.
summary: Schottenheimer said the Giants loss fell well short of the team's standard, but he still believes in the defense's expectations and points to youth and inexperience as the cause. Malik Hooker has a fracture that needs surgery the next day, with an expected recovery window of about two weeks. Overshown has a hamstring strain that also looks like one to two weeks, with nothing long term. With Overshown out, the staff will shuffle linebackers: Devin Winters is the most experienced, Jaishawn Barham got valuable snaps and made good plays but has things to fix, Shemar James is a trusted, smart player, and practice-squad elevations Curtis Robinson and Justin Barron are in the mix, with Barron held to high expectations. He said Caleb Downs can move around but the team prefers him near the line of scrimmage. He credited the Giants' physical run game and misdirection, and said communication breakdowns, offside and taunting penalties, and missed tackles were self-inflicted problems. He defended the fourth-and-short decision on the opening drive and said the offensive line did well in pass protection but was penetrated in the run game. He expects more from Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark and praised Donovan Ezeiruaku's rushes and Cobie Durant's play. He said the team will play young players this week and that the pass rush can be effective once it gets into better down and distance. The next game is against Washington.

title: Shane Steichen: Week 1 Recap, Colts vs. Ravens
headline: Steichen calls Week 1 loss to Baltimore 'extremely disappointing' in all three phases; CJ Allen still sidelined in development, Alec Pierce says he's good to go.
summary: Steichen said that after watching the tape, the Colts were extremely disappointed in all three phases of the Week 1 loss to Baltimore. On the defensive communication issues before the snap, he said it's a team-wide problem, not one player, and that getting back to the huddle quickly and getting checks at the line are what need work in practice. On pass protection, he credited Baltimore's single-bracket pressures and edge blitzes but said the problems are correctable and expressed confidence in the protection schemes. title: WATCH: The Mike McCarthy Press Conference Show presented by PNC (Week 2 at Patriots)
headline: T.J. Watt is the clear defensive star, with snaps capped near 40, and Joey Porter Jr. remains on a ramp-up with no firm return date.
summary: McCarthy said the Week 1 win over Atlanta mattered because it set a standard of play, but he called the offense "herky jerky" and said the team still has a lot to fix. He was most pleased with the four-minute run-game drive and felt the running backs needed about ten more attempts to find rhythm. Third down was the offense's main problem: the team converted just 3 of 13, and he also flagged the one giveaway and poor ball carriage. On defense he praised T.J. Watt as the most impactful player in the game and gave him a game ball, while noting Watt was projected for roughly 40 snaps along with Alex Highsmith and others on the edge. He singled out Cam Heyward's three batted passes and said he played hard. On Joey Porter Jr., McCarthy said the decision to hold him out was his own, that the plan is to increase his work with the trainers and staff on Wednesday, and that he expects him to play once the ramp-up is complete. He declined to say how Porter's absence affected zone-versus-man usage and called the business or contract situation an individual matter. Michael Pittman was praised for making the most of his chances, especially a key crossing route. The next game is at New England on Sunday at 1:00.

title: Todd Bowles on Bucs vs. Bengals: Josiah Trotter's Impact | Press Conference
headline: Bowles says Benjamin Morrison played very well filling in, and Josiah Trotter made a real impact in his debut, while Baker Mayfield's turnovers and the pass rush need to improve before Cleveland.
summary: Bowles said Jacob Parrish has a back sprain, with negative X-rays and MRI, and that it is mainly a matter of working through soreness. He praised Benjamin Morrison's relief work, saying he prepared all week and tackled and covered well when he entered. He was critical of the pass rush, saying the linemen and edge rushers played as individuals rather than together. He said Baker Mayfield knows he must protect the football, and he expects improvement this week. Bowles declined to grade offensive coordinator Zac Robinson after one game, but said he likes where Robinson is and that the offense can be effective if it avoids turnovers. He said Alex Anzalone was rusty and missed some tackles and zone-drop assignments, but expects a bounce-back. On Chris Godwin Jr., he said he played hard and winning football, though the team lost. Bowles said Emeka Egbuka is still working back from missed time and that a fuller practice schedule should help. He praised Bucky Irving's sharp running but wants better ball security. Bowles called Josiah Trotter a real football player who made an impact and will keep improving. He said Rueben Bain's mental approach slipped and Yaya Diaby played hard, and that the group must improve up front. He said Ted Hurst played fast and hard and was open when targeted, and that coverage dictated his targets. Bowles said the team must clean up small details and communicate better, and that Mayfield's focus will be taking care of the ball before the Browns.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Cedric Gray (concussion protocol) is expected back for Week 2 vs. Philadelphia, Carnell Tate got strong early reviews, and Cam Ward's play was called 'not good' overall.
summary: Saleh said the Titans' Week 1 performance against the Jets was poor across all three phases, and he took accountability for the defense, the goal-line personnel mistakes, and the kicking game. He credited Jets coordinator Frank Reich's run-heavy approach (40 rushes) and said the Titans' early-down failures led to fewer run attempts. On Cam Ward, he said the QB is much improved in the pocket and showed progress with his feet early, but needs to deliver more throws and trust his process for 60 minutes. He framed Ward's struggles as a collective issue, citing protection breakdowns and an overall lack of stability after seven coordinators in seven years. Carnell Tate had his best game in a Titans uniform, playing fast and physically in the run game, and Saleh hopes he gets more targets. Anthony Hill flew around, controlled the huddle well, and showed range, while Saleh said he thinks Cedric Gray has cleared concussion protocol and should be good for Week 2. The team will focus on one main correction at a time while still addressing everything else, with a fuller breakdown of what must be fixed coming Wednesday before the Eagles game.

The team will spend the week correcting the main issues before Wednesday's tape session, with the focus on what it takes to win in all three phases. Philadelphia is next Sunday.

title: HC Dan Quinn | 09/13/26
headline: Quinn says Jayden Daniels is back from injury and the offense's turnovers and penalties, not scheme, are the main fixes; no injury details beyond Daniels were given.
summary: Quinn opened by saying the division loss stings and pointed to miscues, especially penalties and explosive plays allowed on third downs, as the key problems to fix before Week 2. He said it was good to have Jayden Daniels back and that Daniels showed good lessons in throwing the ball away and avoiding a sack-type mistake. On Stefon Diggs, Quinn praised his competitive edge and said the team needs to balance the run game with the passing game to create more explosive plays. He said he had a conversation with Diggs after a penalty on a try for two, noting Diggs knows better in that situation. Quinn called the red-zone shovel pass a sound play that was undone by interior penetration, and said the call was one the team had practiced. He flagged frequent snap penalties as a discipline issue he wants answers on, and said the crowd noise did not seem to be the cause. On Terry McLaurin, he said the receiver stayed focused despite getting few targets early, and that the team has to keep spreading the ball since defenses are clouding him. Quinn said he had little injury information to share beyond a couple of players who did not finish the game and promised an update later.
